metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Mongolia

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive and comparative results for Mongolia from the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking assessment (15-year-olds). The factsheet does not provide the technical sampling/weighting variable names (e.g., student design weights or replicate weights), nor does it describe whether analysts applied complex survey weights in the reported estimates. PISA results are produced using the PISA international database procedures that account for the complex two-stage sampling design and, for achievement scales, the use of plausible values; however, this factsheet focuses on published international estimates rather than re-estimation details. For replication or secondary analysis, analysts should use the official PISA 2022 database weights and replicate design information as provided in the PISA technical documentation and apply the same PV methodology for creative thinking scores.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because the document is a country factsheet summarizing published PISA 2022 creative thinking results (means, proficiency shares, and relative performance), rather than reporting an original student-level predictive model with an explicit PV-combining procedure. Missing-data handling is not reported because the factsheet does not describe any re-analysis pipeline or imputation/deletion strategy; it reports OECD-produced estimates based on the PISA database processing. This is therefore a reporting/secondary-use limitation rather than a documented methodological gap in an ML study.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports that in Mongolia, 6999 students in 195 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 40 800 15-year-olds (an estimated 87% of the total population of 15-year-olds). It does not specify additional analytic exclusions beyond the standard PISA implementation and the fact that the creative thinking results are reported for the PISA 2022 creative thinking test administered to participating 15-year-olds in Mongolia.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Mongolia’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking assessment for 15-year-olds. The creative thinking test contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Mongolia’s mean creative thinking score is 25/60, significantly below the OECD average (33), and students’ relative performance is below expectations based on mathematics but above expectations based on reading. The factsheet reports proficiency distributions (54% at least Level 3; 8% at Level 5–6) and within-Mongolia gaps by socioeconomic status (advantaged students +9.5 points) and gender (girls +3.6 points). It also highlights that relative strengths are greater in evaluating/improving ideas and in written/visual/scientific problem-solving contexts, with weaker relative performance in generating diverse ideas and in tasks combining social and scientific problems. The document is descriptive and does not provide an ML modeling pipeline, PV-combining details, or missing-data strategy for re-estimation.
